title: Which format to choose
cards/0/title: No best format, only the right one
cards/0/body:
3D printing needs only the shape: STL or 3MF.
Web and AR on Android: glTF/GLB. AR on iPhone: USDZ.
Animation between programs: FBX.
Scans: PLY.
Large studio scenes: USD.
cards/1/task: A part for 3D printing: only the shape matters. Pick the simplest format for printing.
cards/2/task: A scan with a color at every point. Find a simple format, with no scenes or animation, that keeps vertex colors.
cards/3/task: A character with PBR, animation and a camera for AR on iPhone. Everything has to survive.
cards/4/q: A model from Blender has to go on a website. Put the steps in order
cards/4/items/0: Check the scale and up axis
cards/4/explain: Correct units first, then the delivery format, then compression and display.
cards/5/q: Match each task to a format
cards/6/q: Why does an FBX → OBJ → FBX round trip damage a model?
cards/6/options/0: OBJ stores no hierarchy or animation, so they are lost for good in the middle step
cards/6/explain: Conversion can only lose data. You cannot get it back.
cards/7/q: A client sent an STL and asks you to “color and animate it”. What do you say?
cards/7/options/0: STL has no colors, UVs or skeleton: we need the source in a format with materials and animation
cards/7/options/1: I will convert it to FBX and everything will appear
cards/7/explain: You can turn an STL into an FBX, but it will contain the same bare shape.
